research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from player talent and role counts
talent control in lineup-level influence measures
methodological_questions: Does lineup role coverage vary within team once talent is controlled?
Is role coverage separable from talent and role counts, or does it collapse onto them?
Does talent adjustment behave as intended for lineup-level role coverage measures, given few team-level units?

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality vs talent as predictor of series wins. Record states corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124; after RS net-rating talent control the adaptation term was p=0.275 (per-series logistic), team-in-series cluster adapt p=0.2449; talent stayed significant (p=0.0095 cluster). Record concludes n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality. Tagged A_unanswerable with LIM:confounding, LIM:small_sample, RISK:CONFOUNDING, RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Series-level AVOID share vs winning. Game-level rho=-0.19 p=0.008 recorded as inflated by n and team-quality confound. Series-level rho=-0.26 p=0.07 at n=50; record states ~80 series needed for p<0.05. Verdict recorded as inconclusive.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type. Reports lineup-cell PPP gaps for named initiators (e.g., Jokic vs MIN 0.814, -0.385, n=59) from the possession graph with min-15 gating on play types. Record notes no placebo or matching and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Validation status not recorded.

Sequence-memory lag effects with game-state controls. Naive lag-1 play-type effects were reported as real, but DRIVE lag-1 MWU p=0.0000 became ctrl_p=0.0911 and PNR naive p=0.031 became controlled 0.136 once game-state and within-team baselines were applied. Lag-2 and lag-3+ effects near zero. Verdict null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether an adaptation/coaching measure predicts outcomes after controlling for team talent, using series-level logistic and cluster models.
failed_approaches.why: After talent control the adaptation term was not significant (p=0.275; cluster p=0.2449); the record attributes this to too few series (n~55) to separate the measure from roster quality, and correlation between talent and the measure (+0.124) was non-trivial.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level AVOID-share vs winning test, with a game-level version.
failed_approaches.why: Game-level result was inflated by the number of games and confounded by team quality; series-level result (p=0.07, n=50) was underpowered by the record's own estimate and still confounded by team quality.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Identifying lineup and forced-play-type suppressors for named stars from the possession graph.
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching; record notes later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts. Mechanism recorded as unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Naive play-type lag effects on possession PPP.
failed_approaches.why: Effects for DRIVE and PNR lag-1 disappeared under game-state controls and within-team baselines, which the record classes as artifact (C_artifact).

evidence_establishes: Within this project's retrieved records, every study of a role- or style-type measure against outcomes either was untestable, inconclusive, or an artifact once talent or game-state controls were applied.
Team-quality/talent confounding is a recorded and recurring threat to influence-style measures in this project's data.
Series-level samples of about 50-55 were recorded as too small to separate a coaching or style term from talent.
Naive possession-graph gaps without placebo or within-team baselines were recorded as unreliable.
evidence_does_not_establish: Nothing retrieved tests lineup role coverage (organizer, shaper, terminal) directly, so the role-coverage construct, its within-team variance, and its separability from talent remain untested here.
The retrieved records do not show whether a lineup-level (rather than series- or team-level) unit can achieve adequate power for talent-adjusted role-coverage effects.
No retrieved record reports a validation of the role labels or of the derived play-type classification.
Whether the talent control works for lineup-level role coverage is not shown; the retrieved talent controls were team-level net rating.
own_inferences: The question has three conjuncts. The within-team variation claim is the most testable, because lineup-level possessions (420,993) provide far more units than the 50-55 series in the retrieved studies.

Separability from talent is the hardest conjunct: if role coverage is built from the same player-usage data that determines talent, the measure may be partly derived from talent, and a talent control may remove signal rather than confound it.
Talent control at team level with only 90 team-seasons is likely to be weak; the retrieved records suggest the same issue.
Lineup-level observations within a team share players and minutes, so they are not independent, which would inflate apparent significance unless clustered by team-season and lineup.
uncertainties: Full text of FAM:SF-APPS-027 and FAM:SF-CHT-037 was cut in the retrieval; findings above rely on the summary text only. I did not read them in full.
Record SF-CHT-037 reports sample_and_power as NOT_RECORDED; SF-CHT-009 has no validation record.
Units stated as 90 team-seasons match three complete seasons (2022-23 to 2024-25) at 30 teams each, so the 2025-26 regular season may not be included in that count; this is unverified.
The definitions of organizer, shaper, and terminal, and the talent measure to be used, are not given in the task or retrieved records.
Playoff data are sparse and partly incomplete for 2025-26 before 2026-06-21; the design below keeps them out of the primary test.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show the same kind of question (a style/role measure after talent control) repeatedly ended untestable, inconclusive, or artifact at series or team level. That justified narrowing the question to the within-team lineup-level test, adding placebo and game-state controls, and requiring a separability check before any talent-adjusted claim, rather than proceeding on the question as posed.

blocking_constraints.text: Role coverage is built from the same player-usage and lineup data that determine talent; talent control may remove the signal being tested or fail to remove confounding, and team-level net-rating control has already been recorded as insufficient (SF-APPS-027).

Team-level units (90 team-seasons) and series-level units (about 50-55) were recorded as underpowered for talent-adjusted tests; only lineup-level possessions give adequate units for the within-team claim.
Organizer, shaper, and terminal labels are not defined in the available materials and no label validation is recorded.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests lineup role coverage. Related earlier studies tested coaching adaptation, AVOID share, star-initiator suppressors, and play-type lag effects against outcomes. These were untestable, inconclusive, not hypothesis tests, or artifacts once talent or game-state controls were applied. They partly answer the talent-confounding part of the question by showing the recurring failure mode, but not the role-coverage question itself.

risks.text: Talent and role coverage may be correlated (SF-APPS-027 recorded corr +0.124 for a related measure), so talent control may not isolate role coverage.
Team-level and series-level units are too few for talent-adjusted inference; the lineup-level test must carry the power.
Many lineups have few possessions; role-coverage values for low-minute lineups will be noisy, and the min-15 gate used in SF-CHT-009 may still leave sparse cells.
Role coverage per lineup may not be stable across games or seasons; reliability is not established in any retrieved record.
If organizer, shaper, or terminal labels depend on points or assists (outcome-linked), coverage will be mechanically correlated with efficiency.
Play-type and initiator labels from the play-by-play-derived graph may be misassigned, and no validation is recorded.
SF-CHT-009 reported lineup-level star gaps without placebo; a placebo role assignment is needed for any positive result.
Three roles, several talent controls, and multiple seasons create many comparisons; SF-CHT-037 shows effects shrinking under controls.
Role labels built from full-game or full-season play-by-play may use information after the lineup's possessions.
Possessions with no shot or no assist may give mechanically floor-level coverage values.
Lineup role coverage may have a skewed base rate (most lineups cover few roles), which can distort tests of separability.
Play-type usage and rules changed across 2022-23 to 2025-26; pooled seasons may conflate trend with role effects.
The derived play-type graph and possession records were built by the project pipeline; mismatches between play-by-play and graph counts are not checked in any retrieved record.

design.estimand: Within-team, lineup-level association between role coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal on court) and possession-level points per possession, after talent adjustment; plus a separability check that role coverage is not explained by talent or role counts (partial R2 and variance inflation).
design.unit: Lineup-stint or lineup-possession-block within team-season, with team-season and lineup as clustering levels.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular seasons (90 team-seasons, 420,993 possessions as recorded). 2025-26 regular season only if complete (from 2026-04-13) and reported as a holdout. Playoffs excluded from the primary test.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum-possession gate per lineup, then a power calculation on the within-team variance component; report the minimum detectable within-team effect. If power is not reached, report untestable rather than a null.
design.controls: Talent measured from prior-season or out-of-sample player metrics to avoid leakage; role counts; minutes; game state (period, clock, score margin); opponent lineup strength; within-team baselines. Role labels fixed before analysis and validated against a hand-labeled subset.
design.falsification: Placebo role assignments (shuffled labels within team-season) and a pre-season-only role definition must show no association; a 2025-26 holdout must reproduce the sign and magnitude.
design.multiplicity: Single primary contrast (within-team organizer/shaper/terminal coverage effect); secondary contrasts Holm-adjusted across the three roles and talent specifications.
design.decision_rule: Claim within-team variation only if the primary within-team effect survives the placebo and holdout checks and the separability check shows partial R2 for role coverage above a pre-specified threshold beyond talent and role counts. Otherwise report untestable or uncertain, not supported.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons; 2025-26 regular season only after completion (2026-04-13); playoff files excluded from primary analysis; snapshot date 2026-07-13.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
